(i) the pandemic is expected (by our respondents) to have very large economic costs, (ii) the expected costs have increased over time and (iii) uncertainty about these costs is very large.
(i) the expected output loss of the pandemic is substantial and (ii) the expected output losses are amplified and brought forward in time by the uncertainty about the pandemic.

the pandemic is likely to have a large and persistent impact on the economy and that monetary policy can play an important role in mitigating the costs of this shock.
